economics_heading: The economics: free validation, paid graduation
economics: Prototyping here costs $0 against the same illustrative $0.80/task PAYG reference — every 100 prototype tasks avoids ~$80 of paid inference while you validate reasoning and tool-call behaviour.
The value is information, not just savings: confirming that Kimi K3's reasoning traces drive your agent correctly is worth more than the avoided spend, because it de-risks the later paid commitment.
Budget the graduation: a prototype doing 120 tasks/mo that moves to a $40/mo subscription breaks even at 50 tasks against the $0.80 reference — plan that migration cost from day one.
Do not price production on free quota. Account-variable limits mean this page cannot promise a ceiling — your console's numbers are the only ones that count.

faq.q: Is Kimi K3 on NVIDIA Build really free?
faq.a: For development and prototyping within your account's limits, yes — $0 in the Sep 6 2026 snapshot. Limits vary by account, so confirm your quota in the official console.

faq.q: Do reasoning and tool calls work on the free route?
faq.a: Yes — reasoning and tool-call behaviour is preserved, which is what makes this route useful for validating agents before paying for serving.

faq.q: Can I run production on it?
faq.a: No. This is a development/prototyping allocation with variable, unpublished-per-account limits and no production SLA. Move serving traffic to paid terms.

faq.q: Why won't you quote the exact quota?
faq.a: Because limits vary by account and change over time — any single number here would mislead half our readers. Test your ceiling in the console on day one.

faq.q: Which AI coding tools are actually free with no credit card, and what are the limits?
faq.a: Two routes are free at the point of use in our Sep 6 snapshot: this NVIDIA Build K3 dev access and the Zen Muse Spark $0 promo. Whether signup requires a card varies by account and region, so we do not promise card-free onboarding. Limits differ: account-variable quotas here, a promo window that can end there.
